name: Gammatone
description: Single gammatone bandpass filter (sc3-plugins). Approximates the frequency selectivity of a haircell site on the basilar membrane in the cochlea, following V. Hohmann, 'Frequency analysis and synthesis using a Gammatone filterbank' (Acta Acustica 88, 2002, 433-442). Centre frequency and bandwidth cannot be modulated.

inputs.name: centrefrequency
inputs.description: Centre frequency in Hz — cannot be modulated

inputs.name: bandwidth
inputs.description: Bandwidth of the filter in Hz — cannot be modulated

name: HairCell
description: Simple cochlear hair cell model (sc3-plugins). Positive input opens ion channels at rate minrate+(input*rate); when accumulated chemicals reach 1.0 the cell fires (output 1.0) then decays each sample by the loss factor. The chemical store is replenished at restorerate; spontaneousrate sets a baseline firing rate; boostrate is how much the input drives chemical flow.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Input to be processed (basilar membrane motion at a particular point pulling an inner hair cell's stereocilia)

inputs.name: spontaneousrate
inputs.description: Spontaneous (baseline) firing rate in Hz — how often the cell fires with no external input

inputs.name: boostrate
inputs.description: Amount that input boosts the chemical flow rate leading to cell fire

inputs.name: restorerate
inputs.description: Rate at which the chemical store is replenished, in Hz

inputs.name: loss
inputs.description: Per-sample decay factor applied after the cell fires

name: Meddis
description: Meddis cochlear inner hair cell model (sc3-plugins). Implements Meddis, Hewitt & Shackleton, 'Implementation details of a computation model of the inner hair-cell/auditory-nerve synapse' (JASA 87(4), April 1990). Hard-coded for the medium-spontaneous-rate parameters; output is scaled by 100 from the JASA paper for sensible audio levels. Functionally similar to half-wave rectification plus low-pass filtering, with a more physiologically plausible mechanism.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Input to be processed (basilar membrane motion at a particular point affecting an inner hair cell's stereocilia)
